chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Furat, from Ali ibn Matar, from al-Sakan al-Khazzaz, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is a right upon every adolescent male during every Friday to trim his moustache and his nails, and to touch himself with something from the perfume; and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), whenever it was the day of Friday and there was no perfume with him, would call for one of the headscarves of his wives, moisten it with water, then place it upon his face.'

key_terms.مُحْتَلِمٍ: Adolescent male who has reached puberty

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended grooming practices for men on Friday according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Friday grooming etiquette (sunan al-fitr) as a communal marker of purity and distinction for males who have reached puberty. It specifically notes the use of perfume, with the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) practical adaptation of using a water-moistened headscarf (khumur) when scent was unavailable, emphasizing the spirit of freshness over material necessity. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on personal hygiene as an act of worship and social dignity, particularly in preparation for congregational prayers.
